title: Early plant composition departures gave no clear prediction gain across plots at 17 transplant gradients
abstract: We tested whether an early departure from the cold-to-warm control line predicted a later departure in separate plots. We used 35 TransPlant contrasts in 17 gradients and seven countries. Whole plot histories stayed in training or test sets. With half the plots for training, adding the early vector increased held-out squared error by 5.2% for cover (95% gradient bootstrap gain limits -14.1% to +1.1%) and 4.3% for occurrence (-8.9% to -0.3%). Bounded coefficients gave similar results. A sensitivity test added after these results used all but one plot for training. Cover gain was +0.2% (-2.0% to +2.9%) and occurrence gain was -0.2% (-1.3% to +0.9%). Thus the primary error penalty depended on training size, but neither design gave a clear gain. This limits a fixed early departure as a practical predictor. It does not show that final departures are absent or identify their cause. Small samples, plot dependence, short experiments and test noise limit inference. Code, aggregate evidence, a figure, hashes and retrieval instructions are included. Source records stay external.

display.caption: Prediction gain across separate plots. Positive values indicate lower squared error. Limits resample whole gradients. The two split schemes have different test noise.
